title: Global Youth Climate Training Programme 2026: Fully Online Free Climate Policy & Advocacy Training for Young People Worldwide – How to Apply, Eligibility, Benefits, Timeline, and Deadline
summary: The Global Youth Climate Training Programme (GYCT) 2026 is now accepting applications from young people around the world who are passionate about climate action, environmental sustainability, and international climate policy. Designed as a free, fully online capacity-development programme, GYCT provides participants with an opportunity to deepen their understanding of global climate governance, international negotiations, and practical climate advocacy while learning directly from experienced experts and climate negotiators. As climate change continues to shape the future of every country, empowering young people with the knowledge and skills to participate meaningfully in climate discussions has become increasingly important. The Global Youth Climate Training Programme serves as a gateway for emerging climate leaders who want to contribute to national, regional, and international climate initiatives. Whether you are already involved in climate activism or are just beginning your journey into environmental advocacy, this programme offers valuable learning opportunities that can strengthen your ability to engage in climate-related decision-making and policy discussions. What is the Global Youth Climate Training Programme (GYCT)? The Global Youth Climate Training Programme (GYCT) is an international online learning initiative that equips young people with essential knowledge about international climate policy, climate negotiations, and practical advocacy skills. The programme is designed to ensure that participants understand how international climate agreements are negotiated and implemented while also developing the confidence to advocate effectively for climate solutions within their communities and beyond. Unlike many climate education programmes that require travel or expensive participation fees, GYCT is completely free and delivered entirely online, making it accessible to participants from around the world. The programme also reflects a commitment to inclusivity by providing closed captions during sessions and offering live interpretation in selected languages for the main training sessions. Why You Should Apply Climate change remains one of the world s most pressing challenges, and young people continue to play a significant role in shaping climate action across local and global platforms. Participating in GYCT can help you: Build a strong understanding of international climate policy. Learn how global climate negotiations operate. Develop practical climate advocacy skills. Gain insights from experienced climate experts. Network with young climate leaders worldwide. Improve your understanding of the United Nations climate process. Prepare for future participation in climate conferences and advocacy initiatives. Become better equipped to contribute to environmental policy discussions in your country. Programme Structure The 2026 edition has been carefully designed to combine expert-led learning with more specialized mentorship opportunities. Phase One: Four Expert-Led Sessions The main programme consists of four online expert-led sessions scheduled to take place between: 2 September 2026 – 22 September 2026 These sessions will: Be conducted online. Be delivered in English. Include closed captions. Offer selected live interpretation services, including Spanish. Be recorded and later released publicly. These sessions are open to programme participants and focus on strengthening participants knowledge of climate governance, policy, and advocacy. Phase Two: Advanced Negotiator Alumni Pathway Following the main programme, 20 selected participants will be invited to join an exclusive learning pathway facilitated by Global Youth Coalition (GYC) and Youth Negotiators Academy (YNA) negotiator alumni. These additional sessions will run between: 29 September 2026 – 13 October 2026 The advanced pathway includes: Three additional online sessions. Instruction in English. Closed captions. No live interpretation. Sessions will not be recorded. Because only 20 participants will be selected, this component provides a more personalized learning experience with experienced climate negotiators. Learning Experience Participants can expect an engaging and interactive learning environment that emphasizes both theory and practice. Throughout the programme, learners will: Explore international climate agreements. Understand global climate governance. Learn practical advocacy techniques. Gain knowledge from leading experts. Discuss current climate challenges. Engage with fellow young climate advocates from different countries. Build skills useful for future climate leadership opportunities. Language Accessibility GYCT seeks to make learning accessible to a global audience. Main Sessions Participants will benefit from: English instruction Closed captions Live interpretation in selected languages Spanish interpretation Public recordings after the sessions Additional Sessions Selected participants joining the alumni pathway will receive: English instruction Closed captions No live interpretation No recordings Opportunity to Stay at the GYC House During COP31 An exciting feature of the programme is that GYCT participants will have the opportunity to apply to stay at the GYC House in Antalya during COP31 . This presents an additional opportunity for participants interested in engaging more closely with international climate events and networking with fellow youth climate leaders. However, acceptance into the training programme does not automatically guarantee accommodation. Financial Support The programme is offered completely free of charge. Additionally: Future bursaries may become available. Participation-support opportunities may be announced separately. Financial assistance depends on available funding. Applicants should note that: Applying to GYCT does not guarantee financial support. Any bursary opportunities will be communicated separately if funding becomes available. Programme Funding The organizers note that the programme depends heavily on community support and donations. Due to funding limitations: The 2026 programme includes fewer training sessions than previous editions. Language interpretation options are more limited. Community donations help keep participation free for young people worldwide. Those who are able are invited to support the programme through its fundraising campaign to help expand future access. Key Dates Activity Date Applications Open Currently Open Application Deadline 10 August 2026 (23:59 BST) Main Sessions Begin 2 September 2026 Main Sessions End 22 September 2026 Additional Negotiator Sessions 29 September – 13 October 2026 How to Apply Applicants are expected to complete the online application form by answering questions briefly and accurately. The organizers emphasize that: Most questions are structured. Responses should be concise. Short written responses are requested only when necessary. The application process is designed to ensure fair and efficient screening. Applicants are therefore encouraged to: Read every question carefully. Provide truthful information. Keep written responses concise. Submit the application before the deadline. APPLY HERE Benefits of the Global Youth Climate Training Programme Successful applicants will benefit from: Free participation. Fully online learning. Expert-led climate policy sessions. Practical climate advocacy training. International networking opportunities. Exposure to experienced climate negotiators. Closed-caption accessibility. Selected language interpretation. Opportunity to compete for the exclusive negotiator alumni pathway. Opportunity to apply to stay at the GYC House during COP31. Potential future bursary opportunities, subject to funding. Who Should Apply? This programme is ideal for: Young climate advocates. Environmental activists. Students. Youth leaders. Community organizers. Individuals interested in international climate policy. Young professionals working in sustainability. Anyone wishing to strengthen their climate advocacy skills. No previous experience as a climate negotiator is mentioned as a requirement, making the programme accessible to motivated young people eager to learn. Visit HERE to learn more about the Global Youth Climate Training Programme 2026 Application Deadline The deadline to submit applications is: 10 August 2026 at 23:59 BST Late applications are unlikely to be considered. Interested applicants should prepare and submit their applications as early as possible to avoid last-minute technical issues. Conclusion The Global Youth Climate Training Programme 2026 represents an outstanding opportunity for young people to build meaningful knowledge of international climate policy, climate negotiations, and advocacy without any financial cost. Through expert-led online sessions, networking opportunities, and an exclusive advanced pathway for selected participants, GYCT equips future climate leaders with practical skills that can strengthen their impact at local, national, and international levels. For young people committed to environmental sustainability and global climate action, this programme provides an accessible platform to gain valuable insights, connect with like-minded peers, and prepare for future leadership opportunities within the global climate movement. Interested applicants should ensure they submit their applications before 10 August 2026 at 23:59 BST . title: Africa Education Teachers’ Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded Pulitzer Center Fellowship for Teachers in Africa with Monthly Stipend
summary: The Pulitzer Center has officially opened applications for the Africa Education Teachers’ Fellowship 2026 , an exciting six-month professional development opportunity designed to empower primary and secondary school teachers across Africa. This unique fellowship equips educators with the practical knowledge, teaching strategies, and mentorship needed to integrate journalism into classroom learning, helping students develop critical thinking, media literacy, civic engagement, climate awareness, and ethical media consumption skills. The fellowship is a hybrid program that combines virtual learning, classroom implementation, peer collaboration, and action research. Selected teachers will also receive a monthly stipend to support the implementation of innovative classroom projects while becoming part of a growing network of education leaders across the African continent. If you are a teacher passionate about education, journalism, literacy, media education, environmental awareness, or climate education, this fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity to transform your teaching practice while contributing to the future of education in Africa. About the Pulitzer Center Africa Education Teachers’ Fellowship The Africa Education Teachers’ Fellowship is a six-month hybrid professional development program created by the Pulitzer Center to strengthen teaching and learning across African schools through journalism-based education. The fellowship recognizes that journalism can be a powerful educational tool that helps students: Develop critical thinking abilities. Improve literacy and communication skills. Become responsible consumers of information. Understand environmental and climate issues. Participate actively in civic life. Learn ethical media practices. Rather than focusing solely on traditional classroom instruction, the fellowship encourages teachers to use investigative learning, storytelling, questioning, evidence-based discussions, and media analysis to enrich students educational experiences. Participants will engage in both online and classroom-based activities throughout the fellowship period while collaborating with educators from multiple African countries. Fellowship Objectives The fellowship seeks to build a community of innovative educators capable of integrating journalism into teaching and learning. Its major objectives include helping teachers: Incorporate journalism into classroom instruction. Strengthen students media literacy. Improve critical thinking among learners. Foster civic participation and responsible citizenship. Increase awareness of environmental and climate issues. Promote ethical media consumption. Encourage inquiry-based and evidence-driven learning. Ultimately, the fellowship aims to prepare educators who can inspire students to think critically about the world around them. What Fellows Will Learn Throughout the six-month program, selected teachers will gain practical knowledge and professional skills in several important areas, including: Journalism in Education Participants will learn how journalism can become an effective classroom teaching tool by encouraging students to: Ask meaningful questions. Investigate issues. Evaluate evidence. Verify information. Develop informed opinions. Media Literacy Teachers will learn strategies to help students: Recognize misinformation. Evaluate media sources. Understand digital media. Become responsible media consumers. Critical Thinking The fellowship emphasizes classroom activities that help students: Analyze complex issues. Solve problems creatively. Make evidence-based decisions. Engage respectfully in discussions. Civic Engagement Participants will explore methods that encourage students to become informed and active citizens capable of contributing positively to their communities. Climate and Environmental Education Teachers interested in rainforest conservation, environmental sustainability, and climate education will gain practical classroom approaches for teaching these important global topics. Classroom Innovation Educators will develop creative classroom projects that combine journalism with existing curriculum subjects to create more engaging learning experiences. Fellowship Structure The Africa Education Teachers’ Fellowship is delivered through a hybrid model that combines virtual learning with practical classroom implementation. The program includes: 1. Virtual Learning Sessions Participants will attend online learning modules led by experienced facilitators. 2. Classroom Implementation Teachers will apply newly acquired skills directly in their own classrooms through journalism-based learning activities. 3. Peer Learning Participants will collaborate with teachers from different African countries to exchange ideas, experiences, and best practices. 4. Action Research Teachers will evaluate and reflect on how journalism-based teaching influences student engagement and learning outcomes. 5. Professional Networking At the end of the fellowship, participants will become members of an expanding network of innovative educators across Africa. Benefits of the Fellowship Successful applicants will receive numerous professional and financial benefits throughout the fellowship. These include: Six months of structured professional development. Hybrid learning experience combining online sessions and classroom practice. Mentorship from experienced educators. Guidance from professional journalists. Opportunities to design innovative classroom projects. Participation in collaborative peer-learning activities. Membership in a growing continental network of educators. Monthly stipend to support classroom project implementation. Enhanced teaching skills in journalism and media literacy. Professional recognition through participation in a prestigious Pulitzer Center initiative. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is specifically designed for active teachers who are passionate about improving classroom learning through journalism and media education. Applicants should demonstrate interest in one or more of the following areas: Journalism Literacy education Media education Rainforest education Climate education Environmental education Applicants should also demonstrate a strong commitment to: Fully participating throughout the six-month fellowship. Completing all fellowship activities. Implementing journalism-based classroom projects. Eligible Countries Applications are invited from primary and secondary school teachers currently working in the following African countries: Burkina Faso Cameroon Democratic Republic of Congo Ethiopia Ghana Nigeria Uganda Zambia The fellowship welcomes applications submitted in either: English French Fellowship Duration The fellowship will run for: Six months During this period, fellows will participate in professional learning, classroom implementation, mentoring, collaboration, and project development. Fellowship Format The program follows a hybrid format , consisting of: Virtual learning sessions Classroom practicum Collaborative learning Mentorship Action research This flexible structure allows teachers to continue working while participating in fellowship activities. Cohort Size The 2026 fellowship will select: 10 teachers Due to the limited number of available places, applicants are encouraged to prepare strong applications that clearly demonstrate their commitment to education innovation. Why Journalism Matters in Education The Pulitzer Center believes journalism is more than reporting news—it is a powerful educational approach that encourages curiosity, evidence-based thinking, responsible citizenship, and informed decision-making. Through journalism-based teaching methods, educators can help students: Ask better questions. Evaluate information critically. Identify misinformation. Understand global issues. Become active citizens. Develop communication skills. Strengthen literacy. Engage with environmental challenges. These competencies are increasingly important in today s rapidly changing information landscape. Click HERE to read more. Monthly Stipend One of the unique advantages of this fellowship is that selected participants will receive a monthly stipend to support the implementation of their classroom projects. This financial support enables fellows to translate their learning into meaningful educational activities that directly benefit students. For inquiries, applicants may contact: eselemani@pulitzercenter.org Subject line: Africa Education Teachers Fellowship – [Your Name] Application Deadline The deadline for applications is August 10, 2026 . Interested teachers are strongly encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues. Click HERE to apply. Conclusion The Pulitzer Center Africa Education Teachers’ Fellowship 2026 offers an exceptional professional development opportunity for African educators seeking to transform their teaching through journalism, media literacy, civic engagement, and climate education. Through expert mentorship, collaborative learning, classroom innovation, and financial support, the fellowship equips teachers with practical tools to inspire critical thinking and responsible citizenship among students. With only 10 fellowship positions available , this highly competitive program provides not only valuable professional growth but also the opportunity to join a continent-wide network of forward-thinking educators committed to improving education across Africa. title: Google News Initiative AI Skills Program 2.0 Opens Applications for Journalists in India
summary: The Google News Initiative (GNI), in partnership with How India Lives, has opened applications for the AI Skills Program 2.0 , an advanced training initiative designed to help journalists and media professionals in India integrate artificial intelligence into newsroom operations. Building on the success of the inaugural 2025 edition, the six-week program goes beyond introducing AI tools by equipping participants with practical skills to build AI-powered newsroom applications, dashboards, and workflows that improve reporting, editing, research, and content production. The program begins with a two-day, in-person AI Design Lab in Delhi-NCR on August 10–11, 2026 , where participants will receive hands-on training using Google s latest AI technologies, including Gemini, AI Studio, NotebookLM, Veo, Flow, Stitch, and SynthID. This is followed by five advanced online learning sessions and five weeks of personalized one-on-one mentoring to help participants implement AI solutions within their own newsrooms. Participants will explore AI applications in story research, document analysis, newsroom productivity, content creation, AI agents, and AI-assisted app development through vibe coding—no prior coding experience is required. Each participant will also complete a capstone project that addresses a real newsroom challenge using AI. The first edition of the program produced more than 240 AI-powered newsroom projects, over 100 AI applications, and helped participants save an average of eight hours of work each week. Applications are open to journalists, editors, newsroom leaders, social media teams, visual journalists, and digital publishers working with eligible Indian news organizations. Applicants should have at least 10 years of newsroom experience, be able to attend the in-person workshop in Delhi-NCR, and commit approximately four hours per week throughout the six-week program. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with the final application deadline set for August 5, 2026 . title: Innovate Africa Challenge 2026: Smart Africa and FAO Launch 3rd Edition for AI-Driven Climate-Smart Agriculture Startups in Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda and Uganda
summary: Applications are open for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 (3rd Edition), a major continental innovation initiative jointly organized by Smart Africa and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) to accelerate the deployment of Artificial Intelligence solutions that address agricultural and climate challenges across Africa. Under the theme “From Ideation to Deployment,” the third edition marks an important shift from developing promising technological concepts toward deploying practical, scalable, and context-validated AI solutions capable of delivering measurable benefits to African farmers. The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 is specifically seeking startups, innovators, and solution developers working on AI-driven solutions for climate-smart agriculture. The selected solution will move beyond experimentation or pilot-stage development and be deployed within a Smart Africa Member State in collaboration with relevant government ministries, the Smart Africa Secretariat, FAO country offices, and technical experts. The challenge focuses particularly on AI applications for precision agriculture, crop yield forecasting, pest and disease surveillance, climate risk modelling, adaptive agricultural decision-making, and water and natural resource optimization. Importantly, this edition is geographically targeted. Applications are only open to eligible applicants from Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, and Uganda. Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 at a Glance Key details of the third edition include: Organizers: Smart Africa and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) Edition: Third Edition Theme: “From Ideation to Deployment” Main Focus: Artificial Intelligence for Climate-Smart Agriculture Eligible Countries: Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, and Uganda Target Applicants: Startups, innovators, and solution developers Geographic Focus: Africa Main Objective: Deploy a proven and scalable AI-driven agricultural solution in a Smart Africa Member State Priority Areas: Precision agriculture, crop forecasting, pest and disease surveillance, climate risk modelling, decision support, and natural resource optimization Application Deadline: No application deadline is stated in the information provided About the Innovate Africa Challenge The Innovate Africa Challenge is a continental initiative created to advance technological innovation and accelerate the practical application of solutions capable of addressing major development challenges across Africa. The third edition is jointly organized by Smart Africa and FAO and concentrates on one of the continent s most important intersections: Artificial Intelligence, agriculture, food systems, and climate resilience. Africa s agricultural sector faces significant and interconnected challenges. At the same time, rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence, digital agriculture, data-driven technologies, and related innovations provide new opportunities to improve agricultural productivity, sustainability, resilience, resource management, and access to markets. A persistent challenge, however, is moving technological innovations beyond the pilot stage. Many potentially valuable solutions are developed and tested on a limited scale but are never successfully integrated into national agricultural systems or deployed widely enough to deliver meaningful benefits to farmers. The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 seeks to address this gap. Rather than focusing exclusively on generating new ideas, the third edition emphasizes identifying technologies that have already demonstrated potential and helping move them toward practical deployment and validation. 2026 Theme: “From Ideation to Deployment” The theme of the third edition is: “From Ideation to Deployment” This theme captures the central ambition of the 2026 challenge. The organizers are seeking to move beyond promising ideas toward solutions that can operate effectively in real agricultural environments. The challenge therefore places considerable emphasis on technological maturity, practical implementation, contextual relevance, measurable impact, and scalability. Successful solutions should be capable of producing meaningful outcomes for farmers, agricultural extension services, government institutions, or other stakeholders in African agricultural systems. Why the Innovate Africa Challenge Matters Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform African agriculture. AI-powered agricultural technologies can potentially help farmers and institutions: Make better agricultural decisions Optimize inputs Improve resource efficiency Predict crop yields Detect pests and diseases earlier Respond to climate risks Improve water management Strengthen food security Reduce agricultural losses Improve climate resilience Increase agricultural productivity Despite this potential, promising innovations frequently struggle to transition from prototypes and pilots to large-scale implementation. Another challenge identified by the initiative is that innovations are sometimes developed without sufficient validation within the realities of African smallholder farming. A solution that performs effectively in one technological or agricultural environment may not automatically work in settings characterized by unreliable connectivity, incomplete datasets, diverse languages, different agro-ecological conditions, and predominantly smallholder farming systems. The third edition of the Innovate Africa Challenge therefore emphasizes deployment and real-world validation. Building on Previous Innovate Africa Challenge Editions Previous editions of the Innovate Africa Challenge demonstrated the potential for Artificial Intelligence to contribute to climate action and agriculture. However, the third edition recognizes that demonstrating technological potential alone is not sufficient. Many innovations still require deeper validation within African smallholder farming environments before they can achieve widespread adoption and sustainable impact. The 2026 edition consequently seeks to bridge the gap between innovation and implementation by supporting a solution that can be deployed, validated, and demonstrated under real-world conditions. Main Objective of the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 The central objective of the third edition is to identify and support a proven AI-driven solution for climate-smart agriculture and facilitate its deployment within a Smart Africa Member State. The selected solution is expected to be implemented through collaboration involving: National ministries responsible for Agriculture National ministries responsible for ICT National ministries responsible for Innovation Smart Africa Secretariat FAO country offices FAO technical experts Other relevant ecosystem stakeholders This collaborative structure is intended to provide the institutional environment required to move an AI solution from a promising innovation toward meaningful implementation. Expected Outcomes of the Challenge The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 is designed to produce three broad outcomes. 1. Deployment of a Scalable and Context-Validated AI Solution One proven AI-driven solution will be selected, customized to African agricultural realities, deployed, validated, and demonstrated in a real-world setting. The implementation is expected to contribute to measurable improvements in areas such as: Farmers decision-making Agricultural productivity Climate resilience The deployment should also establish a foundation for potential wider adoption across Smart Africa Member States. This is an important distinction of the third edition: the challenge is not simply searching for interesting AI ideas. It seeks a solution capable of demonstrating practical value in an authentic agricultural context. 2. Stronger Ecosystem and Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration The initiative seeks to strengthen collaboration between the various institutions and stakeholders required for successful digital agricultural transformation. These may include: Technology innovators Government ministries FAO country offices Private-sector organizations Research institutions Farmer organizations Agricultural stakeholders By connecting these actors, the challenge aims to reduce institutional silos, encourage knowledge exchange, strengthen capacity, and establish an enabling environment for sustained digital transformation in agriculture. 3. Evidence Generation and a Replicable Scale-Up Model Another important expected outcome is the generation of practical evidence from the deployment process. Lessons learned from implementation should help create a replicable model for scaling AI-driven climate-smart agriculture solutions across Africa. Such evidence could contribute to: Policy development Investment decisions Responsible AI adoption Digital agriculture strategies Wider technology deployment Future agricultural innovation programmes The long-term objective is to amplify the benefits of responsible AI technologies for African farmers and food systems. Priority Areas for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 The challenge identifies several primary areas of interest. 1. Precision Agriculture and Input Optimization Solutions may use AI and data-driven technologies to help farmers make more precise decisions about agricultural inputs and resources. The objective is to improve resource efficiency while reducing negative environmental impacts. Potential applications could support better agricultural decision-making around the use and allocation of farm resources. 2. Crop Yield Prediction and Forecasting The challenge is interested in AI solutions capable of supporting crop yield prediction and agricultural forecasting. Improved forecasting can contribute to: Proactive agricultural planning Better decision-making Food security Risk management Reliable predictions can help farmers, governments, and agricultural institutions anticipate challenges and make more informed decisions. 3. Pest and Disease Surveillance, Detection and Early Warning Pests and diseases can cause substantial agricultural losses. The challenge therefore welcomes AI solutions that strengthen: Surveillance Detection Early-warning capabilities Timely agricultural responses Earlier identification can allow farmers and agricultural institutions to respond before problems become more widespread. 4. Climate Risk Modelling and Adaptive Decision Support Climate variability and extreme weather conditions increasingly affect agricultural production. AI technologies capable of modelling climate risks and providing adaptive decision support can help strengthen farmers resilience to climate-related shocks. The challenge seeks solutions capable of translating climate and agricultural information into actionable guidance. 5. Water and Natural Resource Optimization Efficient management of water and other natural resources is essential to sustainable agriculture. AI-powered solutions that improve resource optimization therefore fall within the challenge s priority areas. Deployment and Validation Requirements The Innovate Africa Challenge places strong emphasis on technologies capable of operating within actual African agricultural conditions. Participating startups are expected to demonstrate that their solutions can generate reliable and actionable outputs for one or more of the following: Farmers Agricultural extension services Agricultural institutions Solutions should be capable of functioning effectively within challenging and diverse environments. Solutions Must Address African Agricultural Realities The proposed technology should demonstrate its ability to operate in environments characterized by several important realities. Smallholder and Informal Farming Systems Smallholder farmers constitute an important part of African agriculture. Solutions should therefore be relevant to farming environments that may differ substantially from highly industrialized agricultural systems. Partial or Low-Frequency Data AI solutions often depend on large amounts of high-quality data. However, agricultural data in some settings may be: Partial Incomplete Irregular Collected at low frequency Solutions should demonstrate an ability to operate effectively under these constraints. Mobile-First and Low-Connectivity Environments Digital solutions intended for African farmers should account for differences in connectivity and technology access. The challenge specifically recognizes environments where mobile devices may be the primary digital platform and internet connectivity may be limited. Multilingual and Heterogeneous Data Environments Africa is characterized by significant linguistic, cultural, agricultural, and data diversity. Proposed technologies should therefore demonstrate an ability to function in multilingual and heterogeneous data environments where appropriate. Diverse Agro-Ecological Zones and Farming Practices Agricultural conditions differ significantly across countries and regions. Solutions should be capable of adapting to diverse: Agro-ecological zones Cropping systems Farming practices Environmental conditions Integration with National Systems The challenge is particularly interested in solutions capable of integration with: National agricultural extension systems Government ministry systems Existing agricultural institutions This integration component is crucial to moving innovations beyond isolated pilots toward broader institutional adoption. Who Can Apply for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026? The challenge is open to: Startups Innovators Solution developers Applicants must be actively developing or deploying AI-driven solutions for climate-smart agriculture . The challenge is not solely evaluating the technical sophistication of applicants. Applicants are also expected to demonstrate: Technological maturity Commitment to strengthening the innovation ecosystem Potential for measurable impact Viable pathways toward scaling Financial sustainability Click HERE to submit your application Eligible Countries The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 is specifically restricted to applicants from five African countries: Ghana Kenya Malawi Rwanda Uganda The source explicitly states that the call is only open to applicants coming from these countries. Applicants outside these five countries should therefore not assume eligibility for this particular edition based solely on the challenge s broader continental objectives. Additional Eligibility Criteria The source provided introduces a section stating that applicants must meet additional criteria, but the actual criteria following that heading are not included in the supplied information. Prospective applicants should therefore carefully review the complete official challenge documentation before submitting an application to confirm all organizational, technical, operational, financial, or other eligibility requirements. Responsible AI, Data Protection and Governance Requirements All participating startups must comply with important principles governing data use and Artificial Intelligence. Data Protection and Privacy Participants must comply with applicable data protection and privacy requirements in the countries where they operate. Responsible and Explainable AI Solutions must apply responsible and explainable AI practices appropriate to agricultural decision-making. This is particularly important where AI-generated recommendations could influence farmers production decisions, resource allocation, or livelihoods. Bias Identification and Mitigation Participating startups must demonstrate approaches for identifying and mitigating AI bias. Particular attention should be given to bias related to: Gender Geography Farming systems Farmer Data Rights Participants must respect the rights of farmers whose data may be collected or processed. Appropriate consent must be obtained for data use. Confidentiality All information shared under the challenge must be treated in accordance with applicable confidentiality requirements. Smart Africa also reserves the right to establish and enforce additional requirements relating to: Data governance Responsible AI Information management throughout the challenge. Intellectual Property Rules Participating startups will retain ownership of their pre-existing intellectual property. This means intellectual property developed before participation in the challenge remains with the relevant participant. However, the source establishes additional provisions concerning outputs developed under the initiative. Smart Africa will retain rights over: Challenge outputs Reports Frameworks developed under the initiative Any subsequent scale-up or deployment phase may be governed through separate contractual arrangements. Those agreements may establish specific terms covering: Ownership Licensing Deployment rights Applicants should therefore review all intellectual property and contractual conditions carefully before participating. Collaboration with Governments and FAO A significant feature of the challenge is the planned collaboration between innovators and institutional stakeholders. The selected solution is expected to be implemented alongside relevant national ministries, Smart Africa, and FAO. This structure can help ensure that the technology is not developed separately from the institutions responsible for agricultural policy and implementation. It also provides an opportunity to test whether an innovation can integrate into existing national systems and respond effectively to local agricultural priorities. Why Scalability Matters The ultimate goal extends beyond deploying a single solution in one location. The challenge aims to demonstrate an approach that could provide a foundation for broader adoption across Smart Africa Member States. A successful solution should therefore have the potential to: Adapt to different agricultural environments Serve larger numbers of farmers Integrate with national systems Demonstrate measurable benefits Operate sustainably Support evidence-based policy and investment Provide a model that could be replicated elsewhere Why Startups and AI Innovators Should Consider Applying For startups developing AI solutions for African agriculture, one of the greatest challenges can be moving from product development to meaningful deployment. The Innovate Africa Challenge directly addresses this transition. The selected innovation will have an opportunity to demonstrate its capabilities within a real-world environment and work within a multi-stakeholder ecosystem involving government institutions, international organizations, researchers, farmer organizations, and other relevant actors. For an eligible startup with a mature solution, this provides an opportunity to demonstrate that its technology can generate practical value under African agricultural conditions. Application Deadline The information supplied for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 states August 31, 2026 as the application deadline. Click HERE to submit your application Important Considerations Before Applying Prospective applicants should carefully assess whether their solutions align with the challenge before submitting an application. Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate: A clear AI component within their solution. Direct relevance to climate-smart agriculture. Evidence of technological maturity. Practical value for farmers, extension services, or agricultural institutions. Ability to operate under real African agricultural conditions. Potential for measurable impact. Potential for scaling. A pathway toward financial sustainability. Responsible and explainable AI practices. Compliance with data protection and farmer data rights. Ability to address potential bias. Relevance to one or more of the challenge s priority agricultural areas. Applicants should also carefully examine the complete official documentation because some detailed eligibility criteria referenced by the source are not included in the information provided. Visit HERE to learn more about the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026. Conclusion The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 (3rd Edition) represents an important opportunity for AI startups, innovators, and technology developers seeking to transform African agriculture through practical, scalable, and responsible Artificial Intelligence solutions. Jointly organized by Smart Africa and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the challenge moves beyond the traditional innovation competition model by emphasizing real-world deployment. Under the theme “From Ideation to Deployment,” the initiative seeks one proven AI-driven solution that can be customized, deployed, validated, and demonstrated within African agricultural realities. The challenge is particularly focused on precision agriculture and input optimization, crop yield prediction and forecasting, pest and disease surveillance, climate risk modelling, adaptive decision support, and water and natural resource optimization. Solutions must also demonstrate their relevance to the realities faced by African agriculture, including smallholder farming systems, incomplete datasets, low-connectivity environments, multilingual contexts, diverse agro-ecological conditions, and integration with government and agricultural extension systems. Only applicants from Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, and Uganda are eligible under the geographic restriction stated in the call. Eligible startups and innovators developing mature AI-powered climate-smart agriculture solutions should carefully review the full application requirements, responsible AI principles, data governance provisions, and intellectual property conditions before applying. With its emphasis on deployment, government collaboration, evidence generation, scalability, and measurable farmer impact, the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 provides a potentially significant platform for innovators seeking to move promising agricultural AI technologies from pilots toward wider adoption across Africa. title: Youth Ambassador at the 8th German-Baltic Conference 2026 in Estonia: Apply to Shape Europe’s Future Through Policy and Leadership
summary: Young people across Europe have an exciting opportunity to become part of one of the continent s most influential youth policy initiatives. The German-Baltic Future Foundation (DBJW) has officially opened applications for the Youth Ambassador Programme at the 8th German-Baltic Conference , which will take place in Tallinn, Estonia, from 15–18 October 2026 . The conference offers motivated young Europeans an opportunity to engage in high-level policy discussions, collaborate with fellow changemakers, develop policy recommendations for European institutions, and potentially present their work directly to Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) in Brussels . Unlike many youth conferences, participants will not simply attend presentations—they will actively contribute to developing practical policy proposals addressing some of Europe s most pressing challenges. Applications are open until 2 August 2026 (23:59 CEST). About the German-Baltic Conference The German-Baltic Conference is an international youth policy conference organized by the German-Baltic Future Foundation (DBJW) . The conference brings together young people from across Europe who are interested in democracy, European cooperation, leadership, security, public policy, and civic participation. The conference creates a platform where participants exchange ideas, debate current European challenges, and jointly create policy recommendations intended for European decision-makers. title: Blue Ambition Fund 2026 Call for Applications: Grant Funding for Youth Employment and Sustainable Job Creation in Uganda, Ethiopia, and South Africa
summary: Organizations working to create employment opportunities for young people and women now have an exciting opportunity to secure funding through the Blue Ambition Fund (BAF) 2026 Call for Applications . Managed by the Blue Ambition Fund , which is part of the Wilde Ganzen Foundation in the Netherlands, this funding opportunity seeks to empower organizations that are committed to promoting economic independence, strengthening small businesses, and creating sustainable employment opportunities for marginalized communities. The Blue Ambition Fund supports non-profit organizations and social enterprises that are implementing innovative solutions to address youth unemployment, promote entrepreneurship, and strengthen local economies. Through this open call, eligible organizations from Uganda, Ethiopia, and South Africa are invited to submit concept notes and organizational information for consideration. If your organization is working to improve livelihoods through skills development, business support, entrepreneurship, or employment creation, this funding opportunity could provide the resources needed to expand your impact. About the Blue Ambition Fund The Blue Ambition Fund (BAF) is an initiative of the Wilde Ganzen Foundation , a Netherlands-based organization that works with local partners around the world to support sustainable development initiatives. The Fund is committed to increasing economic independence among marginalized youth aged 15–35 years and women by investing in organizations that create meaningful employment opportunities and strengthen local businesses. Rather than offering direct funding to individuals, the Blue Ambition Fund invests in organizations capable of delivering long-term, sustainable employment outcomes within their communities. The Fund believes that empowering young people and women economically contributes to stronger communities, reduced poverty, inclusive growth, and sustainable development. Objectives of the Blue Ambition Fund 2026 Call The 2026 funding round focuses on supporting projects that deliver measurable improvements in employment and entrepreneurship. Specifically, the Fund seeks organizations that can contribute to the following priorities: 1. Strengthening Small and Growing Businesses The Blue Ambition Fund aims to support organizations that help Small and Growing Businesses (SGBs) increase their capacity and competitiveness. Successful projects should focus on: Building business capacity Improving productivity Supporting business growth Strengthening entrepreneurship Expanding market opportunities Creating sustainable and dignified jobs Organizations should demonstrate how their interventions will contribute to long-term business development while generating employment opportunities for young people and women. 2. Creating Sustainable Employment Opportunities The second priority area focuses on helping young people and women gain meaningful employment through workforce development initiatives. Eligible projects may include: Technical skills training Vocational skills development Soft skills training Career coaching Employment readiness programmes Job placement initiatives Workforce development programmes A key requirement is collaboration with the private sector to ensure that training leads directly to sustainable wage employment. The Blue Ambition Fund places strong emphasis on programmes that move beyond training alone by guaranteeing or facilitating real employment opportunities for participants. Who Can Apply? The Blue Ambition Fund is seeking applications from: Non-profit organizations Social enterprises Applicants should have missions that align with the objectives of the Blue Ambition Fund, particularly those focused on youth employment, women s economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, workforce development, and sustainable livelihoods. Before applying, organizations are strongly encouraged to review the Fund s participation guidelines to determine whether they meet all eligibility requirements. APPLY HERE Countries Eligible for the 2026 Call The current funding round is only open to organizations operating in the following countries: Uganda Ethiopia South Africa Organizations outside these three countries are not eligible to apply under the current call. Focus Areas for Funded Projects Projects should contribute to one or more of the following areas: Youth employment Women s economic empowerment Small business development Entrepreneurship support Skills development Workforce development Technical training Soft skills training Business coaching Employment placement Sustainable job creation Inclusive economic growth Capacity building Funding Timeline Organizations should take note of the important dates for the 2026 application cycle. 1 July 2026 Application window opens. Applicants begin submitting: Organizational details Concept note July – August 2026 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. This means organizations are encouraged to submit their applications as early as possible rather than waiting until the closing date. 15 August 2026 Application deadline. All required documents must be submitted before this date. 1 September 2026 Announcement of shortlisted organizations. Selected organizations will move to the next stage of the application process. September – October 2026 Shortlisted organizations will be invited to submit additional documentation, including: Most recent annual report Financial statements Complete funding application Due diligence assessment Applicants will also participate in a short video interview. November 2026 – January 2027 Successful organizations will: Sign grant agreements Complete contracting requirements Begin implementation with Blue Ambition Fund support Application Process Organizations interested in applying should carefully follow each stage of the application process. Step 1 Read the Blue Ambition Fund participation guidelines thoroughly to confirm eligibility. Step 2 Complete the required Organization Details Form . Step 3 Prepare a Concept Note . The concept note should: Be no more than 1,500 words Clearly describe the proposed project Demonstrate alignment with Blue Ambition Fund priorities Explain expected outcomes and impact Step 4 Submit both documents before the deadline. Applicants must email: Organization Details Form Concept Note to: marit@wildeganzen.nl esly@wildeganzen.nl Submission deadline: 15 August 2026 Visit HERE to learn more about the Blue Ambition Fund 2026 Call for Applications. Why Organizations Should Apply Organizations selected for funding will gain the opportunity to: Expand youth employment programmes Strengthen local entrepreneurship ecosystems Support women’s economic empowerment Increase business productivity Build partnerships with the private sector Deliver workforce development programmes Create sustainable employment opportunities Scale innovative community development initiatives Increase long-term organizational impact Key Themes Supported by the Fund The Blue Ambition Fund promotes projects that contribute to: Economic empowerment Youth employment Women s employment Sustainable livelihoods Entrepreneurship Small business growth Skills development Capacity building Inclusive economic development Job creation Why This Funding Matters Youth unemployment remains one of the greatest development challenges across many African countries. At the same time, women continue to face barriers to accessing decent employment and entrepreneurship opportunities. The Blue Ambition Fund recognizes that supporting organizations working directly with these communities can generate sustainable change by improving skills, strengthening businesses, and creating dignified employment. By investing in local organizations with innovative solutions, the Fund contributes to stronger local economies and more inclusive development. Deadline Application Deadline: 15 August 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications early, as submissions will be reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the application period. Conclusion The Blue Ambition Fund 2026 Call for Applications presents an excellent opportunity for non-profit organizations and social enterprises in Uganda, Ethiopia, and South Africa to secure funding for projects that promote youth employment, women s economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable job creation. Organizations with innovative programmes that strengthen small businesses, build workforce skills, and collaborate with the private sector to create lasting employment opportunities are strongly encouraged to apply. With a structured selection process and a clear focus on long-term impact, the Blue Ambition Fund continues to invest in initiatives that empower marginalized communities and contribute to sustainable economic development. Interested organizations should carefully review the eligibility guidelines, prepare a compelling concept note, and submit all required documents before the 15 August 2026 deadline. title: ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship 2026–2027 at the University of Ghana: Fully Funded Research Opportunity for Early-Career Researchers
summary: The Institute of Statistical, Social, and Economic Research (ISSER) at the University of Ghana has officially opened applications for its prestigious Pre-Doctoral Fellowship 2026–2027 , offering an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers who are preparing for doctoral studies. The one-year fellowship is designed to provide talented early-career researchers with extensive hands-on experience in applied development research while working alongside internationally recognized experts in agriculture, natural resources, food systems, and impact evaluation. Hosted by ISSER under the Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA) of CGIAR , this fellowship provides participants with the opportunity to contribute to globally significant research projects while developing practical research skills, publishing technical papers, and collaborating with international researchers. For graduates interested in pursuing a PhD and building a strong research portfolio, this fellowship represents an excellent stepping stone toward an academic or policy-oriented research career. About the ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship is a one-year research programme that aims to strengthen the research capacity of promising scholars before they begin doctoral studies. The selected Fellow will work under the mentorship of Professor Robert Darko Osei , a member of the Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA) at the University of Ghana. Throughout the fellowship period, participants will contribute to research projects focusing on: Agriculture Agricultural development Food systems Natural resources Development economics Impact evaluation Evidence-based policymaking The programme emphasizes practical research experience through involvement in every stage of the research process—from research planning and design to data collection, statistical analysis, reporting, publication, and dissemination. Fellowship Details Host Institution: Institute of Statistical, Social, and Economic Research (ISSER), University of Ghana Research Partner: Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA), CGIAR Duty Station: ISSER, University of Ghana Fellowship Duration: 1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027 Programme Length: One year About ISSER The Institute of Statistical, Social, and Economic Research (ISSER) is one of Africa s leading research institutions dedicated to advancing knowledge in economics, development studies, public policy, governance, agriculture, and social sciences. Operating under the University of Ghana, ISSER conducts policy-relevant research that contributes to national, regional, and global development. The institute collaborates with governments, international organizations, universities, and development partners to generate evidence that informs policy decisions. Researchers at ISSER frequently engage in multidisciplinary projects addressing Africa s most pressing development challenges. About SPIA (Standing Panel on Impact Assessment) The fellowship is supported through the Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA) of CGIAR. SPIA plays a critical role in evaluating the effectiveness and impact of agricultural research investments across the world. Through rigorous evidence generation and impact assessment methodologies, SPIA helps improve agricultural innovations, food security interventions, and sustainable development initiatives. Fellows joining this programme will have the opportunity to collaborate with researchers working on globally relevant agricultural and development challenges. Objectives of the Fellowship The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship seeks to: Prepare talented researchers for doctoral studies. Build advanced research and analytical skills. Strengthen expertise in development research. Promote evidence-based policy research. Enhance capacity in impact evaluation. Provide exposure to international research collaborations. Encourage publication of high-quality academic research. Develop future leaders in agricultural and development economics. Fellowship Responsibilities Successful applicants will become active members of the SPIA research team and will contribute to multiple research activities throughout the fellowship period. Key responsibilities include: 1. Supporting Scientific Research The Fellow will assist with: Planning research activities Implementing research projects Monitoring research progress Reporting on activities under the SPIA workplan 2. Research Design and Data Management Participants will support: Research design Survey preparation Data collection Data management Data cleaning Quantitative data analysis This provides valuable practical experience in the complete research cycle. 3. International Collaboration The Fellow will collaborate with: SPIA s global research team International researchers Other SPIA Panel Members Such collaborations provide exposure to international research standards and multidisciplinary teamwork. 4. Participation in Research Seminars Throughout the fellowship, participants will: Attend SPIA monthly research seminars Participate in collaborative research meetings Engage in academic discussions Learn from internationally recognized researchers 5. Research Communication The Fellow will contribute to producing: Technical reports Research presentations Policy briefs Academic outputs Other scientific communication materials 6. Academic Publications An important component of the fellowship is scholarly publishing. The selected Fellow is expected to: Contribute to research publications. Produce at least two technical papers during the fellowship period. This publication experience significantly strengthens future PhD applications and academic careers. 7. Administrative Support Additional responsibilities include: Providing project support Assisting with administrative tasks Performing other duties assigned by the SPIA Member Benefits of the Fellowship The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship offers numerous professional and academic advantages. Participants will benefit from: One year of intensive research experience. Mentorship from experienced researchers. Collaboration with international experts. Participation in global research initiatives. Exposure to advanced quantitative research methods. Experience in impact evaluation. Opportunities to publish technical papers. Participation in monthly research seminars. Development of professional research skills. Strengthened preparation for doctoral studies. Networking opportunities with international researchers. Competitive fellowship remuneration based on qualifications and experience. Fellowship Remuneration ISSER will offer the selected Fellow a competitive fellowship package , with remuneration determined according to the Fellow s qualifications and experience. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy the following requirements: Academic Qualifications Applicants should possess: A Master s degree in Economics, Agricultural Economics, or a related discipline. Technical Skills Candidates should demonstrate: Strong quantitative skills. Excellent analytical abilities. Experience in research methodologies. Experience in data collection. Research Interests Applicants should have a genuine interest in: Agriculture Natural resources Food systems Development research in developing countries Professional Competencies Successful applicants should possess: Good communication skills. Strong teamwork abilities. Research writing skills. Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams. Additional Advantage Knowledge or experience in impact evaluation will be considered an added advantage during the selection process. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit the following documents: A cover letter explaining their motivation and suitability for the fellowship. A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV). Copies of academic certificates. Contact information for two academic referees. Applicants should ensure that all documents are complete and professionally prepared before submission. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit their applications electronically. Applications should be emailed to: isser@ug.edu.gh Use the following email subject line: Application – Pre-Doctoral Fellowship at ISSER Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the closing date to avoid last-minute technical issues. APPLY HERE Application Deadline Deadline: Monday, 3 August 2026 Late applications may not be considered. Interested candidates are therefore advised to prepare and submit all required documents before the deadline. Why You Should Apply The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship is more than just a research placement—it is a career development programme designed to prepare future scholars for success in doctoral education and beyond. Participants will gain invaluable experience in applied development research, receive mentorship from leading academics, contribute to internationally significant research projects, and build a strong publication record. The fellowship also offers opportunities to develop advanced analytical skills, engage with global research networks, and strengthen future applications for PhD programmes and research positions. For graduates who aspire to become researchers, economists, policy analysts, or development professionals, this fellowship provides an exceptional foundation for long-term academic and professional success. Visit HERE for information about the ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship 2026–2027 at the University of Ghana. Conclusion The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship 2026–2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for early-career researchers to develop practical research expertise while working with one of Africa s leading research institutions. Through mentorship, international collaboration, publication opportunities, and hands-on experience in development research, Fellows will be well-positioned for future doctoral studies and careers in academia, policy, and international development. If you have a strong background in economics or a related discipline and are passionate about agriculture, food systems, natural resources, and impact evaluation, this fellowship could be the ideal next step in your academic journey. Be sure to prepare your application carefully and submit all required documents before Monday, 3 August 2026 .
